content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose a methods for using a StyleGAN to manipulate ImageNet images to adversarially fool a pertained image classifier.  Their approach, called Adversarial Pivot Tuning (APT) is based on Pivotal Tuning Inversion (PTI).  APT trains a model to find the codes for input to the StyleGAN, as well as slightly alters parameters of the StyleGAN with a the PTI objective and an additional term to fool the pertained ImageNet classifier.  There is extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments shown that highlight various properties of the GAN.  They run user tests to determine the quality of the generated images and whether the manipulations maintain the class of original images that were manipulated by APT.  They also run quantitative experiments to determine whether the images are diverse and whether they are able to fool the pertained classifier that APT was trained against.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1. The paper is very well organized and written.  Everything is clearly explained, argued, and reported.
2. There is a strong review of related work that borrows from a number of different, but related lines of prior research.
3. The experiments are done with clear objectives that align mostly with the claims of the paper.

Weaknesses
1. Ultimately this work borrows heavily from prior work, namely StyleGAN and API.  In terms of methodology, the only novel contribution is the cross entropy term in the training objective that encourages the generator to manipulate images that change the predicted class of the pertained model.  This being the only methodological or theoretic contribution, the paper lack novelty.
2. While extensive, I do not feel the experimental results are particularly compelling.  Namely, the experiments make no effort to distinguish themselves from prior work in using adversarial manipulations to fool a classifier.  In addition, there is no direct comparisons between the manipulations produced by APT and the numerous methods listed in the related work that do something similar.  These two points together make it difficult to understand what specifically this work contributes that prior work does not.
3. It seems that APT is heavily dependent on an existing StyleGAN for a given data set for the method to work.  Because only ImageNet StyleGANs and classifiers are investigated, it is unclear how practical this method is for other image classification problems, especially those with limited data.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity - The paper is especially well written and clear.

Quality - While some of the experimental results are not particularly compelling, the method was well argued and the results were clearly explained.

Novelty -  As stated above, the novelty of the work is limited as it borrows heavily from prior work and makes only a small methodological change.

Reproducibility - Training details for the pertained networks are not provided, though possibly follow from prior published work.  That said, the training procedure and hyper parameters seems sufficiently articulated for reproduction.
content.summary_of_the_review: While I applaud the authors for a very well-written paper, I feel that the contributions of the paper are not sufficient for acceptance.  Because the methodological contribution is minimal, the impact on the paper rests mainly on the empirical evaluation.  As I elaborated on above, I do not feel the experiments were compelling enough to really convince me that this work will have significant practical impact, either.

content.title: Response to Reviewer 69ng
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for the comments. We address the individual concerns below.

> Ultimately this work borrows heavily from prior work, namely StyleGAN and API. In terms of methodology, the only novel contribution is the cross entropy term in the training objective 

While we are inspired by both StyleGAN-XL and Pivotal Tuning Inversion (PTI) our method is not used for generation or image inversion, but rather for fooling a classifier. In particular we use a different set of objectives. In particular, we use guidance from both a classifier as well as a pretrained discriminator. 

> the experiments make no effort to distinguish themselves from prior work in using adversarial manipulations to fool a classifier. In addition, there is no direct comparisons between the manipulations produced by APT and the numerous methods listed in the related work

We thank the reviewer for the comment. Following the review, we conducted the following experiments: First we visually compare ourselves against other baselines: visually (Lin et al 2020) and (Song et al 2018) (see figure 1 and 6) and numerically in Tab. 2. For Tab. 2, we observe that the users had a 90% accuracy when classifying images using our proposed method compared to12.5% and 42.5% for the baseline (95% accuracy is for real images)

> It seems that APT is heavily dependent on an existing StyleGAN for a given data set for the method to work. Because only ImageNet StyleGANs and classifiers are investigated, it is unclear how practical this method is for other image classification problems, especially those with limited data.

Our method can be easily adapted to classifiers trained on different datasets, by using a StyleGAN trained to generate from the corresponding image distribution. We note that StyleGAN-XL has been shown to work for datasets such as FFHQ, CIFAR10, and pokemon in addition to ImageNet.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors propose a new method to perform adversarial attacks on deep image classifiers. The classifiers are trained to be robust against adversarial attacks. They formulate the adversarial attack as a Pivot Tuning Inversion problem: first project the real image to a StyleGAN latent space then optimize StyleGAN network weights to minimize the reconstruction loss as well as the attacking objective.


They study the effectiveness of their attack on PRIME-ResNet50 and FAN-VIT, which are the latest classification networks that are trained to be robust. They measure the accuracy and confidence of the network outputs on real images and perturbed images respectively.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths**

The paper is easy to understand. The method is clear and intuitive: using a generative network to construct the path to perturb a real image for adversarial attacks.

They study the effect of their adversarial attacks on specifically trained networks that are supposed to perform well against perturbations. Results show that the networks may decrease confidence or predict the wrong classes after manipulating the image.

The formulation of the image space makes the attack semantically meaningful. The perturbation is done naturally through StyleGAN space. The perturbed image may look photorealistic, while some hyper-parameter tuning is required.

The perturbation dimension is high, which may contribute to the attack success rate.

**Weaknesses**

The difference between this paper and previous GAN-based unrestricted attacks Is that it also allows fine-tuning of the network weights. As they claimed multiple times in the paper, it allows extracting the full potential of a generative model. However, in my opinion, this is only a way to increase the manipulation space to easier achieve a successful attack; regarding novelty, modifying the GAN weight is also covered by Pivotal Tuning Inversion.

The human perception experiment is flawed:

> Q2: For each generated sample, we first display the real image and the associated class to the user. We then display the generated sample and ask whether the class is preserved. Additionally, we consider if the pretrained classifier misclassifies the generated image.

As the real image is presented first, it adds the confirmation bias to the person; whether the class is preserved is highly subjective and it does not necessarily represent whether human detects the change.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
**Clarity:** The paper is clear and easy to understand.

**Quality:** The paper has an extensive quantitative evaluation of its methods on various aspects, such as diversity, transferability, and ablation study on hyperparameters. The results show that such attack is able to fool classifier networks. However, human evaluation is too weak to support that it can also evade human detection.

**Novelty**: The novelty is limited; the idea of using generative models for unrestricted adversarial attack is not new; the optimization of network weights is also not new (pivotal tuning inversion). The authors combined these two to formulate their method (APT).
content.summary_of_the_review: The biggest concern is that human evaluation is weak and the paper lacks novelty. Human evaluation is important since it is unrestricted modification; due to problems in the question design, Table 4.1 cannot convince me that it can evade human detection. This means we do not know whether it exploits the weakness of the network, or simply just interpolates between the feature space of two classes. For example, if we use this method to generate a dog picture that is classified as a cat, it can look like a half-dog half-cat to humans already, so even a perfect classifier will reduce its confidence or even predicts a wrong class.

content.title: Response to Reviewer 5ugw
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for the comments and for finding our method clear and intuitive. We address the individual concerns below.

> However, in my opinion, this is only a way to increase the manipulation space to easier achieve a successful attack; regarding novelty, modifying the GAN weight is also covered by Pivotal Tuning Inversion.

Regarding novelty, while our method is inspired by PTI, it is different and uses a different set of objectives. In particular, we use guidance from both a classifier as well as a pretrained discriminator. 
Following the review, we compare our method to recent baselines: “Dual manifold adversarial training [(Lin et al 2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.02470)” and “Constructing unrestricted adversarial examples with generative models [(Song et al 2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.07894)” - see Figure 1, 2 and 6. In Tab. 2, we show that our method consistently generates class-preserving manipulations (90% correctly classified images) compared to the baselines (12.5% and 42.5% correctly classified images respectively). We also compare our method visually in Fig.1 to Lin et al. In contrast to Lin et al, our manipulations are of a significantly higher quality and are class-preseving. In Fig. 6 we consider the generations of  Song et al, showing these are of lower quality and not class preserving. 
> The human perception experiment is flawed: ..

> As the real image is presented first, it adds the confirmation bias to the person; whether the class is preserved is highly subjective and it does not necessarily represent whether human detects the change.

We thank the reviewer for the observation. Following the review, we perform another user study with 40 new images per method - those generated by Lin et al., our proposed method and the corresponding real images (Q3). We ask humans to independently classify either the baseline images, generations from our method or real images. We find that our method consistently generates class-preserving images (90% correctly classified images) were real images are classified correctly 95% of the time, please refer to Tab.2 of the revised paper. 

> if we use this method to generate a dog picture that is classified as a cat, it can look like a half-dog half-cat to humans already, so even a perfect classifier will reduce its confidence or even predicts a wrong class.

Thank you for the comment. Following our new human evaluation (Q3) it is unlikely that we generate images that are 50% of one class and 50% of another class.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper focus to generate semantics preserved photo realistic adversarial manipulations to the images to fool ImageNet pretrained classifiers. Authors majorly build their work on top of StyleGAN-XL and GAN inversion method to generate photo realistic images. In addition to the optimizations involved in StyleGAN-XL and GAN inversion, authors propose to further optimize the image to fool a pretrained ImageNet classifier along with the support of StyleGAN pretrained discriminators to make the adversarial manipulations appear real. Authors show that the generated images drop the classifier accuracy over 20% and can also be transferable to other classifiers. The generated images contain minor class preserving realistic manipulations based on visual inspections but succeed to fool the classifier.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. Well written paper
2. Easy to understand
3. Generated images contain realistic adversarial manipulations and succeed to fool the classifier yet remain perceptually like original image.
4. The generated images can also fool other classifiers.

Weakness:
My major concern lies in the novelty of the method. There exists previous works (also cited in Related work section) that uses pretrained GANs to generate images to fool the classifier. The difference is that pretrained GANs in the literature does not manipulate real images. In contrast, StyleGAN-XL in association with GAN inversion method allows real image manipulations. This work replaces pretrained GANs from prior work with StyleGAN-XL and GAN inversion and applies the adversarial objective as seen in prior works to fool the classifier. I am not confident enough to consider a technical contribution from this work. However, I agree that this is the first work to leverage StyleGAN-XL and GAN inversion to manipulate realistic images that fool the classifier.
